library_interface: from fin_skills.algorithms import positions, adjust_prices, run, catalog. positions(algorithm_id, prices, split_factors, *, window=None, parameters=None, lag=1) returns the whole position table: a DataFrame with the same index and columns as prices. It adjusts the prices once (prices*split_factors; the factors are cumulative), computes the position on row t from adjusted closes through row t-1 only, and fills warm-up rows with 0. Portfolio algorithms (inverse_volatility, cross_sectional_momentum) receive simple returns of the adjusted closes; window=N limits each decision to the last N returns. Signal algorithms (ma_crossover, vol_target_momentum) run on each asset and are scaled by 1/number of assets. parameters is a dict passed to the algorithm; pass every value the rule needs that differs from a default. Defaults: cross_sectional_momentum lookback=60, top_k=3 (each chosen asset gets 1/top_k); ma_crossover fast=5, slow=20; vol_target_momentum lookback=20, target_vol=0.10, periods_per_year=252, max_exposure=1.0; inverse_volatility takes none. adjust_prices(prices, split_factors) returns the adjusted closes. run(algorithm_id, data, **parameters) is the lower-level call for ONE decision or ONE asset: data is a dict keyed by the input name, {"asset_returns": DataFrame of simple returns with no missing rows} for portfolio algorithms, returning one allocation, or {"prices": Series of one asset's adjusted closes} for signal algorithms, returning already one-bar-lagged exposures. Guards: from fin_skills.api import get; get("execution_lag").run(fn=callable, df=DataFrame, k=integer) checks that positions through row k do not move when rows >= k change; get("assert_causal").run(fn=callable, df=DataFrame, k=integer) checks features; get("adjustment_check").run(close=Series, actions=[(date, ratio)]) checks a split convention. result.passed is a bool. Guards detect defects; they do not repair data.
primary_endpoint: valid deliverable: accepted by the arm controller and valid under the E4 grading equations and probes (execution, 1e-8 agreement, timing probes k=32,64 including the same session, split invariance)
secondary: grader validity of the final attempt regardless of acceptance
grader validity of the first attempt
strict execution-lag audit of the final program (execution_lag guard, per-asset perturbation, k=32,64; post hoc only)
changes_from_v1: library arm: interface text with the real signatures and data keys, and the positions()/adjust_prices() panel layer documented
library arm: rule cards for the task in the system prompt; failed checks get the cause and rule from fin_skills.api.rules.explain
controller and grading tracers use run(algorithm_id, data, **parameters); positions() is traced as a library call
raw arms: prompts, checks and feedback byte-identical to v1
optional rules_guards arm (rule cards and explained feedback, no library)
limits: Same E4 tasks, seeds, models and grading equations; E4 and v1 failures informed the repairs, so this is not an independent holdout.
Controller checks overlap grader properties (timing, split); only the grader checks numerical agreement with hidden references, with other perturbations.
The library arm changes documentation, rules, enforced library use and checks together; raw_guards isolates the checks and rules_guards, if run, the rules.
Synthetic author-designed rules; three seeds on four fixed rules are not twelve independent problems; two sizes of one model family.
No financial-return or profitability endpoint; one shared GPU allocation.
